claims.headline: Tia-Clair Toomey fuels five-time CrossFit Games titles with a high-protein, whole-food performance diet built around eggs, lean beef, and jasmine rice
claims.body: As a five-time CrossFit Games champion and Olympic weightlifter, Tia-Clair Toomey follows a high-protein omnivore diet that prioritizes whole-food protein sources and complex carbohydrates over processed supplements. In a full-day-of-eating video published on her YouTube channel, she documented daily intake in the 2000-2500 calorie range with approximately 140-150g of protein, 230-250g of carbohydrates, and 65-70g of fat. Staples include scrambled eggs with bacon and a bagel for breakfast, lean ground beef bowls with jasmine rice at lunch, pork tenderloin or beef sirloin at dinner, and oat-banana protein shakes after training. Her approach treats food as performance fuel rather than a rigid diet system, eating to support twice-daily training demands and overnight recovery.

sources.excerpt: Tia-Clair Toomey documents a full day of eating during her CrossFit training block, covering all meals from breakfast through dinner with macro breakdowns.
The six-time CrossFit Games champion shares her high-protein nutrition approach ahead of the 2022 season.

claims.headline: Tia-Clair Toomey on food as fuel: 'I don't restrict — I eat to perform'
claims.body: Rather than following a restrictive eating protocol, Tia-Clair Toomey approaches nutrition as an extension of her training. She avoids cutting food groups and instead focuses on eating enough whole-food protein and carbohydrates to support the physical demands of twice-daily CrossFit and Olympic weightlifting sessions. This performance-first philosophy has remained consistent throughout her championship run — prioritizing recovery and energy over body composition rules.

sources.excerpt: Tia-Clair Toomey discusses her non-restrictive approach to eating and how she structures her nutrition around her training schedule.
